tools.name: get_default_policy
tools.description: Get the default policy document (its keys at their defaults, comments included), as `source`. Every uploaded report must carry a policy file of its repository: write it as hotpath/policy.toml (or hotpath/<benchmark>-policy.toml), edit it, then check it with validate_policy.

tools.name: get_diff
tools.description: Explain what changed in a benchmark: compare a stored report with the baseline recorded for it at upload (the report the PR comment compared), judged under the policy the report carried. tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Fetch one stored report by pull request, commit or id (exactly one). `pr` and `commit` answer the newest matching upload; `commit` matches the measured commit or a PR's head commit, so the local HEAD sha of a PR branch finds the PR's report. tools.name: list_benchmarks
tools.description: List one repository's benchmarks. A repository that does not exist, that the user cannot see or that has no App installed all answer not_found. list_repos already includes every repository's benchmarks; use this one when the repository is known.

tools.name: list_reports
tools.description: List a repository's stored reports, newest first, as summaries without payloads: id, benchmark, commit, PR, event, verdict, dashboard URL and the run's `totals` (wall time, allocated bytes or allocation count, peak RSS, Callgrind instructions and Callgrind wall time, as display strings; null when th

tools.name: list_repos
tools.description: List the repositories the token's user can see with the hotpath GitHub App installed, ordered by full name, each with its benchmarks (name, stored reports, time of the newest report). tools.name: validate_policy
tools.description: Check that a policy TOML document parses as a hotpath policy, with the parser that judges uploaded reports. Stores nothing. A document with a problem is an error naming it. Use it after editing a policy file, before committing it.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Show which user and API token this connection acts as: the GitHub login, the token's name and expiry. Use it to confirm the connection works, or after a call answers invalid_token.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_default_policy, get_diff, get_report, list_reports · Private data: get_default_policy, get_report, list_repos, validate_policy, whoami · Public sink: get_diff, get_report · Destructive: get_report, list_reports.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_default_policy, get_diff, get_report, list_reports · Private data: get_default_policy, get_report, list_repos, validate_policy, whoami · Public sink: get_diff, get_report · Destructive: get_report, list_reports

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
